report.verdict: A pre-revenue pivot quarter: the legacy online-casino book is being run for cash and shrank 51% YoY to $2.4m while ROLR launch spend pushed adj. EBITDA to -$2.1m (vs -$0.2m) and the quarter's cash outflow to ~$4.7m. The equity (EV ~$15m) is now an option on Q4-26/2027 prediction-market traction that management has not quantified, and the $13.4m cash pile covers roughly three quarters at the current burn — so the funding question arrives before the proof point.

kpis.label: Net loss, cont. ops / diluted EPS

summary: **Headline: revenue halved, losses widened, prediction markets still at zero.** Q3-26 net revenue $2.395m (-50.7% YoY from $4.858m; -14.7% QoQ from $2.809m). Loss from operations -$2.7m vs -$0.7m; pre-tax loss -$2.6m vs -$0.8m. GAAP net loss from continuing ops -$2.78m (-$0.25 basic/diluted) vs +$2.88m (+$0.34/+$0.31) a year ago — the prior-year profit was entirely a $3.6m deferred-tax valuation-allowance release at a Maltese subsidiary plus $0.8m of discontinued ops (Casino Room domain). Adj. EBITDA (non-GAAP) -$2.09m vs -$0.16m. ROLR prediction markets contributed $0 revenue in Q3 and 9M.

**Versus expectations: no meaningful consensus exists; the print tracked the Q2 trajectory.** Q2-26 revenue was already -52% YoY, so the -51% is not new information. What is incrementally negative is the QoQ slide in casino volume (UDCs -31%, actives -43%) and the step-up in burn (adj. EBITDA -$2.1m vs -$1.8m in Q2). Shares fell 15.5% to $2.56 in the first session after the release (16 Nov).

**Guidance bridge: no numbers, only a framework — and it got worse on the casino side.** Management gives no revenue/EBITDA guidance. The qualitative framework moved from Q2's 'launch planned' to 'launched 21 Oct; Q4-26 is the first quarter with prediction-markets revenue; 2027 is the first full year and the major growth driver'. New since Q2: the New Zealand exit on 1 Dec (22% of Q3 net gaming revenue) means casino revenue 'steps down further from December with full effect from Q1-27'. Runway language unchanged ('at least the next twelve months') despite cash falling $4.6m in the quarter.

**Casino volume collapse is the division driving the P&L.** Quarterly active users 5,448 (-75% YoY, -43% QoQ); UDCs 4,723 (-77% YoY; 'roughly a quarter' of last year); wagers $53.3m (-64% YoY, -17% QoQ); deposits $8.8m (-63% YoY) and $31.1m for 9M (-56%). First-time depositors down ~95% YoY [per secondary summary of the 10-Q]. Management's preferred metric — revenue per UDC — more than doubled to $507 (from $242) and hold rose to ~4.5% of wagers (~+120bps; 'roughly 35% more on every dollar wagered'), i.e. the book is being harvested, not grown.

**Geographic concentration is extreme and about to get worse.** Finland $1.62m (67% of NGR, -40% YoY), New Zealand $0.52m (22%, -57%), Canada $0.21m (9%, -65%), Norway nil (exited; $0.27m a year ago), rest of world $47k. With NZ gone from 1 Dec, Finland will be ~85% of a ~$1.6m/quarter casino book — and Finland itself transitions to a licensed regime in 2027 (the company's licensing intent there is not disclosed in the materials reviewed).

**Cost base: opex -8% YoY to $5.1m, but the mix has flipped toward ROLR.** Direct operating costs -59% to $0.8m (33.7% of revenue vs 40.8%); G&A +8% to $3.05m (127% of revenue vs 58%); advertising & promotions +84% to $1.0m (42% of revenue vs 11%), of which $541k is related-party (Spike Up Media) vs $92k; product & software development +17% to $247k. Revenue less direct costs of $1.6m covers barely half of G&A.

**Adj. EBITDA reconciliation is clean but the adjustments are modest.** Net loss -$2.78m + SBC $0.42m + D&A $0.10m - net interest income $0.12m + tax $0.18m + FX loss $0.10m = -$2.09m. 9M adj. EBITDA -$5.18m vs -$3.34m; note the Q3 release implies H1-26 adj. EBITDA of -$3.09m vs -$3.11m reported in August (a $19k presentational difference).

**ROLR milestones delivered on the stated cadence.** Invitation-only beta 15 Sep; public launch 21 Oct for eligible US customers; iOS app 9 Nov; Android via Google Play targeted before year-end; NFA commodity-trading-advisor registration obtained ahead of 'a very powerful new product release' promised before end-November. Structure: ROLR US LLC is a guaranteed introducing broker, accounts carried by Crypto.com FCM; CDNA is the exclusive contract provider through ROLR's US technology for the first 24 months from the April 2026 collaboration agreement.

**Strategic optionality is being built — but all of it is contingent.** ROLR FCM LLC formed 11 Nov with Connamara Technologies advising on a potential FCM application (not yet filed); ProphetX commercial agreement (12 Nov) only becomes effective six months after FCM registration; management floated DCM/DCO licences longer term. An FCM would sit outside the Crypto.com exclusivity, which is the real point of the exercise. The 13 Aug DeepEther Labs (mrkts.com) source-code licence gives them ownership of the customer-facing app — the first time they have controlled their own product roadmap.

**Capital position: debt-free but thinning.** Cash & equivalents $13.4m (vs $18.0m at 30 Jun and $2.1m at 31 Dec-25); restricted cash $0.4m; no borrowings; equity $27.3m; 10.99m shares (11.04m at 13 Nov). 9M operating cash outflow -$8.9m (vs -$4.5m), capitalised software/licences -$3.6m (vs -$0.45m), FCF ≈ -$12.5m, funded by $23.5m net equity raised in January ($25.0m registered direct at $13.21 plus $1.0m private placement at $2.80). Q3 alone: ~$4.7m total cash reduction, of which ~$1.7m was capitalised ROLR development.

**Runway maths does not comfortably support 'twelve months' if marketing ramps as signalled.** CEO: 'we're definitely in growth mode… for the moment, we're looking to get out there and spend.' At the Q3 outflow rate (~$4.7m) the $13.4m lasts ~3 quarters; if Q4 A&P doubles, year-end cash is ~$8–9m [our estimate]. Management's assurance presumably assumes ROLR revenue and/or spend flexibility. We regard an equity raise in H1-27 as more likely than not — and the January placement-agent warrant structure (94,625 warrants at $16.51) shows the toolkit.

**Restatement and controls are a governance overhang.** On 16 Oct the company amended its Q1 and Q2-26 10-Qs to reclassify ~$1.0m of placement-agent warrant fair value from G&A to APIC: Q1 net loss restated to $2.0m (-$0.19) from $3.0m (-$0.29); H1 to $4.3m (-$0.41) from $5.3m (-$0.50). No effect on cash, equity or adj. EBITDA. The 10-Q discloses unremediated material weaknesses in ICFR [per secondary summary; Item 4 not read directly].

**Related-party exposure is growing with the pivot.** Spike Up Media (founder-affiliated) received $541k of A&P in Q3 (54% of total A&P; $940k for 9M), plus a $333k related-party prepayment on the balance sheet and $1.6m due to affiliates. A Dawson James analyst explicitly asked whether launch marketing dollars are flowing to shareholder-owned partners (Spike Up, Lines.com, Forever, Leverage); management declined to disclose allocation.

**What management emphasised vs. buried.** Emphasised: revenue-per-UDC doubling, launch cadence, Bernstein's ~$410bn 2026 / $10tn-by-2035 prediction-market volume estimate (via The Block), new hires (CBO Flip Pidot, SVP Product Ben Sutherland ex-Greentube USA CEO). Buried or absent: any ROLR KPI (funded accounts, volume, net revenue, take rate, CAC), the -95% drop in first-time depositors, wagers -64%, G&A rising on half the revenue, and the economics of the Crypto.com revenue share — 'not something that we've disclosed publicly'. First ROLR data is promised with FY results in March 2027.

**Regulatory backdrop cuts both ways.** Casino: exits from Norway (2025), NZ (1 Dec 2026, limited-licence regime), and a Finland licensing transition in 2027 leave an Estonian-licensed book with no obvious growth jurisdiction (an Ontario entity, HRON Services, exists but is dormant). Prediction markets: risk factors flag 'the evolving and uncertain federal and state legal and regulatory environment… including litigation and enforcement actions'; management says the state-by-state marketing plan is built with 'eyes wide open about which states are hot'.

**Market reaction and valuation.** Release hit after the 13 Nov close (regular session -7.1% to $3.03; after-hours -7.3% to $2.81); first full session 16 Nov -15.5% to $2.56. Market cap ~$28m ≈ 1.0x book; EV ~$15m against $13.4m cash. 52-week range $1.16–$33.68 — the stock is ~92% off the January prediction-markets spike at which the $25m raise was priced.

**Thesis read-through: the casino is no longer the story, and it cannot fund the story either.** Casino gross profit of ~$1.6m/quarter is sub-scale against $3.1m of G&A, so the group is structurally loss-making until ROLR revenue appears. The IB model (ROLR earns a share of exchange/FCM fees on customer trading) is capital-light but thin-margin and dependent on Crypto.com for contracts, custody and clearing for two years. Bulls get a live, regulated, owned-code platform with partners and ~$15m EV; bears get -77% UDCs, no ROLR disclosure, a related-party marketing channel, a restatement and a ~3-quarter runway.

**Sector read-across.** A micro-cap pivot into US prediction markets lands into a field where scale players (Kalshi, Polymarket, DraftKings, FanDuel/CME, Robinhood, Crypto.com itself — and 'Meta entered the fray' per an analyst on the call) will set CAC and promo intensity. ROLR's differentiation claim is acquisition-marketing competence from its casino years; the test will be Q4 cohort payback, which we will not see until March.

highlights.text: Casino unit economics have been engineered up: revenue per UDC $507 (+109% YoY, +22% QoQ), hold ~4.5% of wagers (~+120bps), direct costs 33.7% of revenue (vs 40.8%), lifting NGR-less-direct-cost margin to 66% from 59% — gross profit held flat QoQ at $1.6m on 15% lower revenue.

ROLR shipped on the stated timeline — beta 15 Sep, public 21 Oct, iOS 9 Nov, Android targeted by year-end — and Q4-26 becomes the first revenue quarter; with the DeepEther source-code licence they own the front end for the first time.
Balance sheet is debt-free: $13.4m cash, $27.3m equity, $23.5m net equity raised in January; interest income of $115k now offsets part of the loss. EV ~$15m at $2.56.
Opex fell 8% YoY to $5.1m even while absorbing launch costs; direct operating costs -59% show the exited-market cost base has genuinely been removed, not just the revenue.

Regulatory optionality is being built in the right order: CTA registration done, FCM entity formed with Connamara advising, ProphetX signed for post-FCM contract breadth, DCM/DCO floated — an FCM would sit outside the Crypto.com exclusivity.

Senior hires are credible for the pivot: Flip Pidot (CBO, prediction-markets veteran) and Ben Sutherland (SVP Product, ex-CEO Greentube USA), plus Kindbridge responsible-trading framework ahead of scale.

lowlights.text: Casino volume collapse: actives -75% to 5,448, UDCs -77% to 4,723, first-time depositors ~-95%, wagers -64% to $53.3m, deposits -63% to $8.8m; revenue -51% YoY and still -15% QoQ — the decay rate is ~15%/quarter before the NZ exit.

Burn stepped up: adj. EBITDA -$2.1m (vs -$0.2m), operating loss -$2.7m, ~$4.7m total cash reduction in the quarter incl. $1.7m capitalised build; 9M FCF -$12.5m against $13.4m cash — 'at least twelve months' of runway looks dependent on ROLR revenue or spend flexibility, and dilution risk in H1-27 is material.

New Zealand (22% of NGR) exits on 1 Dec with full effect from Q1-27; Finland then becomes ~85% of a ~$1.6m/quarter book while itself moving to a licensed regime in 2027 — licensing intent and tax impact undisclosed.

Q1 and H1-26 10-Qs restated in October (~$1.0m placement-agent warrant cost moved from G&A to APIC) and ICFR material weaknesses remain unremediated — a review failure on a significant transaction at a company about to report a brand-new revenue stream.

Related-party marketing: founder-affiliated Spike Up Media took $541k (54% of A&P) vs $92k a year ago, plus a $333k related-party prepayment and $1.6m due to affiliates; management would not disclose the allocation of launch spend to shareholder-affiliated partners when asked on the call.

Zero ROLR disclosure — no funded accounts, volume, take rate, CAC or Crypto.com revenue-share terms — with first data promised only at FY results in March 2027; 24-month CDNA exclusivity caps contract breadth until an FCM is (maybe) obtained.
G&A rose 8% to $3.05m (127% of revenue) and SBC was $0.42m on a $2.4m revenue base; fixed overhead is roughly 2x casino gross profit, so the group is structurally loss-making until ROLR scales.

forecast.intro: There is no numeric guidance to bridge — High Roller has never issued revenue or EBITDA targets. The qualitative framework moved in three ways versus the August (Q2) framing. First, ROLR went from 'planned launch' to launched (beta 15 Sep, public 21 Oct, iOS 9 Nov), so Q4-26 is confirmed as the first quarter with prediction-markets revenue and 2027 is positioned as 'the major growth driver'. Second, the casino outlook deteriorated: the New Zealand exit on 1 Dec (new since Q2; 22% of Q3 NGR) means casino revenue 'steps down further from December with full effect from Q1-27', on top of a ~15%/quarter organic decay. Third, spend intent firmed up — 'we're definitely in growth mode… looking to get out there and spend' — while the liquidity assurance ('sufficient… for at least the next twelve months') was simply repeated despite cash falling from $18.0m to $13.4m in the quarter. The division driving the near-term P&L is therefore the casino on revenue and ROLR on cost; the only division that can change the trajectory is ROLR, and it has no disclosed KPIs.

forecast.view: **Q4-26E: revenue ~$2.2–2.6m (-55% to -60% YoY vs a ~$5.5–6m Q4-25 base we have not verified), adj. EBITDA -$3m to -$4m, margin below -120%.** FY26E revenue ~$10.8–11.2m and adj. EBITDA ~-$8.5m to -$9.5m on our arithmetic (9M actual $8.57m / -$5.18m plus the Q4 range). **Leverage direction: net cash shrinks from $13.4m toward ~$8–9m at year-end and ~$4–5m by mid-2027 absent ROLR revenue or a raise; there is no debt and we would not expect any — the funding route is equity, and the January placement-agent/warrant structure is the template.** For 2027 the casino book is ~$1.5m/quarter and falling, so group revenue is essentially ROLR's commission share of customer trading on CDNA contracts: at an assumed IB take of a few basis points of notional, the platform would need hundreds of millions of dollars of quarterly contract volume to replace even the lost casino revenue — an outcome that is possible in this market but unproven for a sub-scale, single-exchange IB competing against Kalshi, Polymarket, DraftKings, FanDuel/CME and Robinhood for the same CAC. Swing factors, in order of importance: (1) ROLR funded accounts, volume and net revenue per account in the March FY print; (2) the Crypto.com revenue-share and whether an FCM registration is actually pursued (it would change the economics and the capital need); (3) Q4 marketing intensity and the related-party share of it; (4) the Finland licensing decision for 2027; (5) state/federal action on sports event contracts, which is the main exogenous risk to the whole model. Our stance: the quarter was as expected on the casino and uninformative on ROLR; the equity trades as a ~$15m-EV option whose first real datapoint is four months away, and the probability of needing to exercise financing before that datapoint is the key risk to the share count.
watch: ROLR KPIs at the FY26 print (March 2027): funded accounts, contract volume, net revenue per account, CAC payback — and whether management commits to a recurring disclosure set
Q4 cash burn and year-end cash vs. our ~$8–9m estimate; any S-3/ATM, registered direct or warrant exercise activity (94,625 placement-agent warrants at $16.51 are far out of the money)
Android app timing (targeted Q4-26) and the late-November CTA-linked product release — what it is and whether it carries incremental regulatory exposure
FCM decision: whether ROLR FCM LLC actually files with the CFTC/NFA; capital requirements; impact on the Crypto.com/CDNA exclusivity and the ProphetX effective date

New Zealand exit mechanics from 1 Dec (player-balance run-off, any retained customers) and the resulting Q1-27 casino base; Finland 2027 licensing — application intent, tax rate and compliance cost on 67% of NGR
Related-party spend trajectory (Spike Up Media A&P, prepayments, due to affiliates) and whether the board provides allocation disclosure after the analyst challenge
Remediation of the two ICFR material weaknesses and audit scope for FY26 given the restatement and a new revenue stream with third-party-carried accounts
Regulatory: state litigation/enforcement on sports event contracts and CFTC posture; any state-level geo-blocking that narrows ROLR's addressable US footprint
Competitive promo intensity in prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket, DraftKings, FanDuel/CME, Robinhood, Crypto.com's own app) and its effect on ROLR CAC

report.sharePriceReaction: Release and call came after the 13 Nov close; the regular session was already -7.1% to $3.03 and the stock slipped a further -7.3% to $2.81 after hours. First full session (Mon 16 Nov): -15.5% to $2.56 (market cap ~$28m, ~1.0x book; EV ~$15m). 52-week range $1.16–$33.68 — ~92% below the January spike at which the $25m registered direct was priced at $13.21.
